hook.en: On the Galapagos Islands, Darwin saw small black birds with beaks of many shapes. Those finches helped him explain how new species arise.
hook.kn: ಗ್ಯಾಲಪಗೋಸ್ ದ್ವೀಪಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಡಾರ್ವಿನ್ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಕೊಕ್ಕಿನ ಸಣ್ಣ ಕಪ್ಪು ಹಕ್ಕಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕಂಡರು. ಅವು ಹೊಸ ಪ್ರಭೇದಗಳ ಉಗಮವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಲು ನೆರವಾದವು.

body.en: Adaptive radiation is the evolution of different species in a geographical area starting from one point and radiating into other habitats. Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands evolved from seed-eating ancestors into insect-eating and other forms with different beaks. Australian marsupials radiated from a common ancestor into many forms. When more than one adaptive radiation occurs in isolated areas, it is convergent evolution: placental mammals in Australia show forms similar to marsupials, such as the placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf.
body.kn: ಒಂದು ಭೌಗೋಳಿಕ ಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಪೂರ್ವಜರಿಂದ ವಿವಿಧ ಪ್ರಭೇದಗಳು ವಿಕಾಸವಾಗುವುದು ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆಯ ಪ್ರಸರಣ. ಉದಾ: ಡಾರ್ವಿನ್ ಫಿಂಚ್‌ಗಳು, ಆಸ್ಟ್ರೇಲಿಯಾದ ಮಾರ್ಸುಪಿಯಲ್‌ಗಳು.

points.en: Placental vs marsupial look-alikes → convergent evolution

body.en: Darwin, after his voyage on HMS Beagle, concluded that existing living forms share similarities with each other and with forms that lived millions of years ago. Alfred Wallace, working in the Malay Archipelago, reached similar conclusions. Their two key concepts are branching descent and natural selection: populations vary, resources are limited, and individuals with useful variations survive and reproduce more (fitness = reproductive fitness). Lamarck had argued that use and disuse of organs drove evolution, such as the giraffe's neck. Hugo de Vries, working on evening primrose (Oenothera lamarckiana), proposed that large mutations cause speciation in single steps (saltation); Darwin's variations, by contrast, are small and directional.
body.kn: HMS ಬೀಗಲ್ ಯಾನದ ನಂತರ ಡಾರ್ವಿನ್ ನೈಸರ್ಗಿಕ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಶಾಖಾ ವಂಶಾವಳಿ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತ ಮಂಡಿಸಿದರು. ವ್ಯಾಲೇಸ್ ಸಹ ಇದೇ ತೀರ್ಮಾನಕ್ಕೆ ಬಂದರು. ಹ್ಯೂಗೋ ಡಿ ವ್ರೀಸ್ ಈವನಿಂಗ್ ಪ್ರಿಮ್‌ರೋಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆಯಿಂದ ಹಠಾತ್ ವಿಕಾಸ (ಸಾಲ್ಟೇಶನ್) ಪ್ರಸ್ತಾಪಿಸಿದರು.

problem.en: Compare how Lamarck and Darwin would each explain the long neck of the giraffe.

steps.en: Lamarck: ancestors stretched their necks to reach leaves; the longer neck acquired by use was passed on.
Darwin: ancestors varied in neck length; those with longer necks got more food, survived and reproduced more.
Over generations the frequency of long necks increased by natural selection. Acquired characters are not inherited, so Darwin's view is accepted.

answer.en: Lamarck: inheritance of acquired characters; Darwin: natural selection of existing variation
